To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for the considered class of tauto-logies the optimal bounds for the following proof complexity measures are obtained: size of proofs, number of inferences, number of occurrences of connectives, number of distinct connectives.

for the class of tautologues of length k ≥ 3 and width w ≥ 1 the following bounds hold: (i) the length of the shortest proof in the considered Hilbert style cut-free system is at least k − 2 and at most k ; (ii) the size of the shortest proof is at least w and at most w + k − 3.

for the considered class of tauto-logies in many valued logic with cyclic negation and implication the optimal bounds for different measures of complexity are: the size of a refutation is O ( n 3 / 2 ), the size of a cut-free proof is O ( n ), and the length of a refutation (the length of a cut-free refutation) is O ( n log n ), where n is the number of variables of the formula.
